data.why: The Walmart deal is a massive operational expansion that directly causes back-office finance work like procurement and AP. It also avoids the generic funding round hook that every other sales rep will use.
data.angle: Building out 300 new delivery sites means manufacturing more drones and infrastructure, leading to a surge in purchase orders and supplier invoices that the finance team has to process.

not_chosen.reason: Every rep will open with the funding round since it was covered by 40+ outlets.
Strategic Finance is usually FP&A, not AP or procurement, making the back-office pitch a stretch.
The 300 new sites expansion is more specific and directly tied to procurement and AP volume.
Too old (over a year) and not a compelling trigger for back-office pain.
Bad news: Mentions a competitor's stock cratering, which is negative and irrelevant.

data.subject: 300 new sites
data.body:
Hi Mac,

Saw Walmart is adding 300 new Zipline delivery sites. Building out that much infrastructure usually means a flood of new purchase orders and supplier invoices. Who is matching all those bills today?

Mindbody processes 95%+ of invoices end to end with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
